# Observer-Separated Two-Time Quantum Dynamics

**Local Horizon Obstructions, Cross-Perspective Consistency, and Finite-Dimensional Evaporation Bounds**

Yohtaro Soga · November 28, 2026

Five conditional finite-dimensional results: autonomous algebra closure versus restriction; energy-moment immunity and local horizon obstructions; complete achievable joint recovery band and shared-record readout; spectral pinching and protected windows; unassisted compression with side-channel controls.

# Research materials

Yohtaro Soga · November 28, 2026

[Research overview](../README.md) · [Reading guides](https://gawakkyu0603-bit.github.io/physics/en/quantum-gravity/ostqd/index.html)

| Resource | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| [Manuscript (PDF)](paper/main.pdf) | 29 pages; 56 cited references. |
| [LaTeX source](paper/main.tex) · [Bibliography](paper/references.bib) | Original source and 3 vector PDF figures. |
| [Lean sources](lean4/) · [Kernel and axiom log](lean4/VERIFICATION_LOG.txt) | 50 audited public declarations in the supplied build. |
| [Numerical code](scripts/verify_ostqd.py) · [Recorded data](docs/numerical_verification.json) | 451 scientific numeric fields, seed 20261126. |
| [Prior literature](PRIOR_ART.md) · [Verification scope](VERIFICATION.md) · [Checksums](SHA256SUMS) | Attribution, analytical boundaries and current file identities. |

## Reproduction

Run on a working copy because Python regenerates the data and figures.

```sh
python -m pip install -r scripts/requirements.txt
OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 python scripts/verify_ostqd.py
```

With elan and the supplied Lean/Mathlib configuration, run `bash verify_lean.sh` from `lean4/`. Compile from `paper/` using `pdflatex main.tex`, `bibtex main`, and two further `pdflatex main.tex` runs. See the verification scope for the exact mathematical hypotheses and analytical boundaries. Cite the manuscript and stable PDF URL (https://gawakkyu0603-bit.github.io/physics/downloads/ostqd.pdf). No new blanket license is assigned.

paper.subtitle: KMS Covariance, Non-Gaussian JT Fluctuations, and Chiral-Horizon Obstructions
paper.author: Yohtaro Soga

summary.en: A thermal open-system continuation of OSTQD: KMS covariance and uniform-contraction tracking, frozen-coefficient JT cumulants and an exactly reversible energy jump model, and the constructive Mellin positive-type extension of a free chiral horizon defect.

general.en: Follow the physical questions behind thermal baths, fluctuating black holes, horizon correlations, and information recovery.

student.en: Work through thermal channel equations, energy cumulants, point-split correlations, and controlled model comparisons.

expert.en: Examine the hypotheses, proof strategies, analytic obstructions, quantitative controls, and formalization boundaries.

en: The guides cover SK normalization, KMS covariance and tracking, JT fluctuation closures and a non-explosive detailed-balance process, the sharp smooth-band contact threshold and non-normal quasifree state, per-port locking and separate scattering and information benchmarks.

The free-current Mellin construction is a positive-type state in the specified model, not a microscopic gravitational mechanism or a universal firewall. General observer instruments and a controlled dynamical endpoint remain open.

paper.title: Observer-Separated Selective Instruments, Born-Weighted Branching, and Non-Isometric Pullback Defects in Type II Gravitational Algebras
paper.author: Yohtaro Soga

summary.en: The third OSTQD study develops selective instruments on causal observer contexts, conditional steering obstructions and Born-weighted branch records, a semifinite entropy split, sharp non-isometric pullback bounds and causal/linear controls on branch coupling.

general.en: Understand ensembles, individual records, correlations, entropy and information recovery.

student.en: Work through quantum instruments, CHSH, trace entropy, polar decomposition and causal channels.

expert.en: Examine the finite-dimensional and semifinite proofs, quantitative sharp bounds and open gravitational bridges.

en: The guides cover observer-poset instruments, conditional state change, Local Friendliness, signed global couplings, contextual Born records, semifinite entropy, sharp polar-isometric bounds, causal sequential emission and five distinct branch-coupling tests.

Finite clock and evaporation examples are not continuum gravitational constructions. The semifinite theorem is analytical; relativistic gluing, gravitational crossed-product instruments, a microscopic branch-transition rate and autonomous matrix evaporation remain open.
